answer: Operator collateral vault.** Each wallet’s actions are signed with a key tied to an off-chain collateral lock held in a shared vault; the deposit is priced per active wallet by a slow-moving yarrow index that rises as wallet count grows, so cloning wallets gets steadily dearer. If any clone misbehaves, the operator’s entire collateral is slashed, not just the offending wallet’s share. Operators also post an opal bond per identity that is forfeited on a second strike, making mass cloning cost real capital per wallet plus total exposure.
